newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal to buy aircraft lighting firm.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal to buy aircraft lighting firm.

text.p: U.S. industrial powerhouse AlliedSignal Inc. announced Wednesday that it agreed to buy Grimes Aerospace Co., which makes aircraft lighting and other aircraft systems, from investment firm Forstmann Little and Co.

AlliedSignal declined to give any details on what price it would pay for Urbana, Ohio-based Grimes. But, in an announcement issued at its headquarters in Morris Township, N.J., and at the Paris air show, it said the deal would not affect its 1997 earnings but would enhance earnings next year.
It also said Grimes Aerospace's current annual sales of $230 million, generated by 1,400 employees worldwide, were growing at a double-digit rate.

Grimes' customers include Boeing Co., Airbus Industrie and other aerospace companies, as well as commercial airlines. Its main facilities are in Connecticut, Florida, South Carolina and Ohio. Privately owned Forstman Little is based in New York.

"Grimes' world-leading aircraft lighting systems are an important addition to our aerospace product offerings, while the valves, heat exchangers and electronic systems will provide us with new product offerings in those industry segments," Daniel Burnham, president of Allied's Aerospace unit, said in a statement.
"Grimes Aerospace's well-managed distribution channels and customer support systems are an excellent fit with our growing after-market parts and repair and overhaul business," he added.
